text:
The conversation around Sidney Crosby this month has been about his future, not his game. TribLIVE's Mark Madden asked whether "the unthinkable" is now thinkable, other outlets have floated options for a Penguins team that keeps losing, and Erik Karlsson's name is all over the trade market. None of that has come from Crosby, who is 39 and has played all 1,440 of his NHL games in Pittsburgh.

The hockey says he's still very good and a little unlucky. He has 13 points in 20 games, which reads as a slow start, but six goals on 7.3 expected and a 52% share of 5v5 expected goals say the process is fine. His points per 60 (1.98) sit well below the range we'd expect from him (2.44 to 3.28). Evolving-Hockey made the same case last season: 2.9 expected wins built from chances against 1.2 actual.

All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists. The passes are still arriving. The question is whether Pittsburgh's finishers, and Pittsburgh's direction, can match them.
headline: Crosby, at 39, amid the noise
